label: Customer name
hint: The account's public name, as executives say it.

label: File slug
hint: Lowercase, no spaces. Used for the output file name and storage keys.

label: Industry
hint: One or two words, used in the disclaimer.

label: Global footprint
hint: Headquarters plus the main hubs and markets, from public sources.
example: Headquartered in Hartford, CT, serving customers in 28 countries. Hubs: a technology campus in Charlotte, NC; claims operations in Jacksonville, FL; asset management in Boston; regional offices in Toronto, London, Dublin, Singapore, Sydney and Manila

label: Audience
hint: Who will watch or play it, by role.
example: Northwind Mutual's CIO, CISO, chief risk officer and the heads of Group Life, Claims and Asset Management, plus the Cisco account team

label: Goal
hint: What the audience should believe or agree to at the end.
example: show that early, cross-domain signals acted on under policy protect renewals, claims experience and regulatory standing, then agree to run discovery on one live mission with its business owner

label: Cisco scenario
hint: The Cisco topic the missions demonstrate.
example: Cisco Cloud Control and AgenticOps, powered by the Splunk-based Cisco Data Fabric

label: Products and capabilities
hint: Comma-separated Cisco and Splunk capabilities to feature.
example: Cisco Cloud Control, AI Canvas, Cisco AI Assistant, Cisco Data Fabric (Splunk), Splunk ITSI, Splunk Observability Cloud, Splunk ES and SOAR, ThousandEyes, Catalyst SD-WAN, Nexus Dashboard, Cisco XDR, Duo, Hypershield, Webex Contact Center

label: Strategy name
hint: Short name of the customer's public strategy, as it reads inside a sentence.

label: Strategy pillars and commitments
hint: Public pillars and numeric targets the missions map to.
example: grow Group Life and Disability; simplify claims; scale the retirement platform; expand in Asia; lower the expense ratio by 80 bps; return $6B to shareholders by 2030

label: Intro headline
hint: A short promise, ending with a full stop.
example: Catch it before your customers ever feel it.

label: Number of missions
hint: Usually 10 (8 to 12 works). One mission per real location.

label: Business functions (filters)
hint: Semicolon-separated lenses for the mission rail. Six works best.
example: Revenue and growth; Customer experience; Operations and cost; Risk and compliance; Security; IT and network

label: Mission locations
hint: Real sites, each with its business unit, and optionally a mission idea and region. Add minor offices for the globe.
example: Hartford (HQ, Group Life open enrollment); Charlotte (technology campus, change risk); Jacksonville (claims, hurricane season); Boston (asset management, market-data microbursts); Toronto (Canadian retail, partner API conversion); London (U.K. pensions, operational resilience); Dublin (EU entity, DORA third-party risk); Singapore (Asia bancassurance, field app); Sydney (group insurance portal peak); Manila (global service center voice quality, security incident in minutes). Minor: Chicago, Phoenix, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Mumbai

label: Build time budget (hours)
hint: How long the coding model should spend. 8 to 16 is typical.
